description: Event delivery semantics — retry policy, dead-letter event, and on_failure callback (Issue #61). Verifies that all subscriber types honor the unified retry config, that permanent failure emits apcore.event.delivery_failed with the normative payload schema, and that the DLQ event itself is not retried.

test_cases.description: A subscriber that fails twice then succeeds MUST receive 3 total delivery attempts (initial + 2 retries) and MUST NOT emit a DLQ event when the third attempt succeeds.
A subscriber that fails on every attempt MUST trigger emission of apcore.event.delivery_failed after max_attempts is reached. The DLQ event payload MUST conform to the normative schema.
If a subscriber registered for apcore.event.delivery_failed itself raises, the SDK MUST log at ERROR and discard. The DLQ event MUST NOT be retried (no infinite loop).
When a subscriber config omits the optional id field, the SDK MUST generate a stable identifier and use it consistently across all DLQ events emitted by that subscriber.

A subscriber's `retry:` block in config MUST reach the delivery policy, for EVERY built-in subscriber type. features/event-system.md documents it under the heading 'showing the policy on multiple subscriber types', and no SDK read it: only the `webhook` factory built a policy, and only from the legacy flat `retry_count`. Two SDKs did not even have a `retry` field on `file` / `stdout` (and `filter` in apcore-rust) for a parser to write into, and apcore-rust's `webhook` wrote `retry_count` to a field its `retry()` never read — so the one spelling that looked wired was inert too. See apcore#85.

`retry_count` is the pre-nested-block spelling and MUST keep working for `webhook` as a deprecated alias, translated as `max_attempts = retry_count + 1`. When both are present the NESTED block wins — it is the documented form and carries all four fields, where the flat one carries only an attempt count.

driver_contract.assert_a_policy_that_differs_from_the_de: Every asserted value differs from the shipped default on ALL FOUR fields (7/250/10000/3.0 against 3/100/30000/2.0). A case whose policy matches any default field passes whether or not the config was read — which is how this defect survived in three SDKs at once.
driver_contract.every_type_or_the_case_is_half_done: Drivers MUST assert all five built-in types. The defect was not uniform: `webhook` parsed a different (flat) spelling, and `file` / `stdout` / `filter` had no field at all in some SDKs. Asserting `webhook` alone would have reported green in every SDK while four types ignored their configuration.
driver_contract.read_the_resolved_policy_not_the_config: Assert the policy the DELIVERY PATH resolves for the subscriber — what the emitter would act on — not the dict the factory was handed. apcore-rust stored `retry_count` on a field its `retry()` never consulted, so a config-shaped assertion was green while delivery used the default.
driver_contract.a_case_must_carry_its_own_inputs: Each subscriber entry carries the fields its type REQUIRES to construct — `url`, `platform_url`, `path`, `delegate_type` / `delegate_config` — not just `type` and `retry`. An earlier revision omitted them and every driver invented its own table. The three happened to agree, so nothing broke — but agreement reached separately by three drivers is not a contract, it is three private guesses that have not diverged yet. The inputs live here so that if an SDK ever spells a required field differently, the case fails instead of each driver quietly compensating.
